correctness.rationale: The graph Laplacian is explicitly diagonalized into constant, within-part, and block-constant eigenspaces with exact projection weights. The resolvent diagonals have a sign-definite difference formula ordered by part size; the smallest diagonal has one quadratic positive zero. Positivity off diagonal follows from the inverse of the irreducible M-matrix. Two symbolic identities and 1,230 exact full-matrix checks over 246 profiles were replayed; finite tests do not prove the all-size statement.

originality.rationale: The 2014 invariance-threshold paper gives broad rational-method sufficient bounds, not a complete-multipartite closed classification. The published general reversible Crank–Nicolson resolvent-return criterion supplies prior matrix identities and spectral crossing facts, but does not evaluate multipartite diagonal weights, prove the sharp minimum-part selector, the partition-independent two-parameter threshold, or fixed-order extremal characterization. Extensive analogous searches in published-finding corpus and literature found no dominating explicit classification; the possibility of unindexed specialist results remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed specialized complete multipartite or complete bipartite CN positivity formula could subsume the exact threshold.

The general published reversible-chain spectral criterion plus known complete-multipartite Laplacian eigenspaces may render some deductions short; novelty asserted only for explicit sharp two-parameter collapse, critical part selector, and fixed-order part-extremality.

value.rationale: The exact full classification replaces graph-size matrix resolvent tests by a closed quadratic in total order and minimum part size for arbitrarily many unequal parts. It identifies which vertices lose positivity, proves strict no-recovery, and characterizes sharp extremizers under fixed graph order and part count. These are motivated natural parameter effects for positivity-preserving implicit graph heat timestepping, not a chosen finite table.
